title: Service failure stereotypes and dashboard stories for inference observability
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Create a taxonomy of recurring inference failure "stereotypes" (time-based, capacity-based, model-rejects, protocol errors) and ship a set of dashboard stories and tracing hook conventions that let oncall and SREs recognize, triage, and mitigate these patterns quickly.
background: We currently have many ad-hoc dashboards and tracehook enrichers that surface symptoms (timeouts, 5xx spikes, high p99). Engineers still manually map symptoms to causes. This ticket codifies a lightweight failure classification ('stereotypes') tied to specific trace attributes, metric signatures, and runbook actions, then implements dashboard stories and tracing hook annotations to operationalize it.
proposed_solution:
- Define a small, orthogonal set of failure stereotypes: TIMEOUT_WAIT, QUEUE_OVERLOAD, MODEL_REJECTION, TOKEN_TRUNCATION, KV_CACHE_MISS_SPREAD, RESOURCE_PREEMPT, KERNEL_OOM, PROTOCOL_BROKEN (HTTP/gRPC status patterns), DOWNSTREAM_BACKPRESSURE.
- For each stereotype, specify: canonical tracespan tags, metric thresholds (token p95/p99, queue length, inflight requests), log signatures, and an ordered remediation playbook (rollback model, scale pool, throttle client, increase sampling).
- Implement tracing-hook enrichment: add span tags model.variant, batch.size, seq.len, kv.cache_hit, backend.backoff_ms, kernel.mem_pressure, request.route_priority. Ensure these tags are low-cardinality when appropriate and gated by sampling policy.
- Create 6 dashboard stories in Console: 1) Stereotype incidence timeline, 2) Per-route SLO exposure by stereotype, 3) Latency surface heatmap annotated with dominant stereotype, 4) Model-error & protocol-failure matrix, 5) Synthetic probe overlay vs production errors, 6) Remediation-playbook quick-actions (links to runbooks/PRs).
- Extend metrics pipeline: add stereotype tag propagation through aggregation keys and wire into SLI/SLO calculation. Adjust log sampling and retention for spans flagged with high-severity stereotypes.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Taxonomy document published and approved by Observability and Runtime teams
A2: Tracing-hook changes deployed in canary (adds required tags with <10% overhead on sampled spans)
A3: Dashboard stories implemented and linked from oncall playbook; each story has an owner
A4: One synthetic probe intentionally triggers each stereotype and produces expected dashboard annotations
A5: SLO exposure shows correct attribution for two month of backfilled data (scripting job)

notes: Keep tag cardinality low: model.variant and route_id ok, avoid attaching full prompt hash. For high-cardinality attributes use hashed buckets (e.g., seq.len_bucket). Consider progressive enrichment: only attach heavy tags for spans already flagged by anomaly detector to limit ingestion costs.
